title: Establish review runbook and handshake protocol for cross-team PRD approvals
creator: Ava Chen
body: Background: Recent PRDs for Dedicated autoscale and Private upgrade experienced multi-week delays due to unclear reviewer responsibilities, missing legal checklist items, and inconsistent handoffs between PM, Design, and Engineering. Goal: define a lightweight, repeatable runbook and ’handshake’ protocol that standardizes how PRDs move through review and sign-off with SLAs, templates, and an escalation path. Deliverables include a Confluence runbook, a PRD template with section-level owners and checkboxes, a Linear review workflow pattern, and a pilot with two upcoming PRDs (Dedicated autoscale and Private upgrades).
acceptance_criteria: Confluence runbook published in /team/prd-governance with versioned changelog and owner
PRD template added to the company template repo with explicit reviewer roles for each section
Linear workflow tags and required-review fields implemented (e.g., @design-review, @legal-ok, @eng-accept) and validated in one test PRD
Defined SLAs for initial review (48 hours) and final sign-off (5 business days) documented and agreed by stakeholders
Escalation matrix (PM -> Product Director -> CTO/Head of Legal) documented and tested during pilot
Pilot run executed with two PRDs and retrospective notes captured with measurable reduction in review cycle time
